Webserver writes PHP/PHAR file to web-accessible upload directory (CVE-2026-48062 polyglot drop) AIInstallation High
Hunts the file-write event characteristic of CVE-2026-48062 exploitation: a CodeIgniter4 (or other PHP) webserver process saves a .php/.phtml/.phar file under public/, uploads/, writable/uploads/ or similar web-served path using the attacker-controlled client filename. This is the dropped polyglot webshell on disk before it gets called. Rationale: Anchored on the article's specific failure mode: `$file->move($path)` preserves the client filename, so an attacker-named shell.php with image bytes ends up on disk in a web-served directory. The combination of (PHP/web-server parent process) + (executable PHP extension) + (web-accessible path) is article-specific and rare in a healthy production system. Cross-checked against GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx (CodeIgniter4 patches in v4.7.3) and CWE-434. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CodeIgniter4 framework cache writes during view compilation (typically land in writable/cache/, not writable/uploads/)
  • Composer install/update writing vendor/* PHP files when the vendor dir sits inside the web root
  • CI/CD deployment pipeline rsync'ing PHP files into /var/www during release
  • Legitimate plugin or theme installation via an admin web UI (CMSes that allow PHP plugin uploads)
  • Developer SFTP uploads to staging when the SFTP daemon runs under the webserver UID
Suppression filter
// Defender refinement — drop framework cache + vendor dir writes
| where FolderPath !contains "writable\\cache" and FolderPath !contains "writable/cache"
| where FolderPath !contains "\\vendor\\" and FolderPath !contains "/vendor/"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "composer" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "artisan"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the dropped file from the host, examine magic bytes vs extension (GIF/JPEG header + `<?php` body = confirmed polyglot). Identify the upload route by correlating webserver access logs (csUriStem with POST) against the file write timestamp. Confirm the app is CodeIgniter4 and check installed version against 4.7.3. 2) Contain: quarantine the file (chmod 000 or move outside docroot), suspend the affected vhost or web pool, block the source IP at the WAF/edge, and patch to CodeIgniter4 >= 4.7.3. 3) Hunt: pivot on the webserver UID for any process spawn in the 60 min after the file write (post-exploit shell). Scan the web fleet for other .php/.phar files written by webserver UID in the last 30d. Grep app source for `$file->move(` calls that don't pass `$file->getRandomName()`.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe","php-fpm","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","php.exe","php","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","caddy.exe","caddy")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|phps|pht|php3|php4|php5|php7)$"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(public|uploads?|wwwroot|htdocs|writable[\\/]uploads?|httpdocs|web|www|html)(\\|/)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd","nginx","apache2","caddy")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","phps","pht","php3","php4","php5","php7")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(public|uploads?|wwwroot|htdocs|writable[\\/]uploads?|httpdocs|web|www|html)(\\|/)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileExtension,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webserver writes PHP file to web-accessible directory (CVE-2026-48062 polyglot drop)
id: 8c9e7af2-3b2a-4d1f-9a4c-2c6a5b1f4d11
description: Detects a PHP/HTTP server process writing a .php/.phtml/.phar file into a web-accessible directory, the on-disk artifact of CVE-2026-48062 exploitation in CodeIgniter4 (ext_in rule trusts MIME-guessed extension, so shell.php with GIF header passes validation and is saved under its original name).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
  - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
author: TI Pipeline
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.008
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\caddy.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phar'
      - '.phps'
      - '.pht'
  selection_dir:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\public\uploads\'
      - '\public\'
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\writable\uploads\'
      - '\wwwroot\'
      - '\htdocs\'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_ext and selection_dir
falsepositives:
  - Application deployment via CI/CD writing PHP files into the web root
  - Composer or package-manager updates updating vendor/ files
  - Legitimate plugin/theme installers writing PHP files via the web UI
level: high

PHP/webserver process spawns shell or recon binary (post-CVE-2026-48062 webshell execution) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the classic web-to-shell process lineage that follows successful exploitation of CVE-2026-48062: php-fpm, php-cgi, w3wp, apache or nginx parent processes spawning interactive shells, recon commands, or LOLBin downloaders. This is the smoking gun of webshell-driven RCE on the host. Rationale: Article-specific because CodeIgniter4 is server-side PHP — successful exploitation lands an attacker in the PHP-FPM / Apache mod_php execution context. The webserver-parent + shell/recon-child lineage is the universal post-RCE behaviour for webshells and is far rarer in a healthy app than a generic 'powershell.exe' alert. Mapped against MITRE T1505.003 (Web Shell) and T1059.003/004 references. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Drupal Drush, Laravel Artisan or WP-CLI invocations spawned from web admin endpoints
  • Legacy applications using shell_exec/system/passthru for image conversion (ImageMagick, ghostscript, ffmpeg wrappers)
  • Health-check probes that run hostname/uname/df via the webserver UID
  • Composer or git commands shelled out during admin-triggered deploys
  • Backup scripts triggered from a PHP admin panel (mysqldump via exec())
Suppression filter
// Defender refinement - suppress known framework shell-outs
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "artisan" and ProcessCommandLine !has "drush" and ProcessCommandLine !has "wp-cli" and ProcessCommandLine !has "composer"
| where not (FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1"))
| where not (FileName in~ ("hostname","hostname.exe","uname") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("health","probe","readiness","liveness"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent's HTTP access log entries around the spawn timestamp - the URI tells you which endpoint hosted the webshell. Inspect the child command line for stage-2 download (`curl`, `wget`, base64 piped to bash). Identify the application and whether it is a CodeIgniter4 site on a vulnerable version (<4.7.3). 2) Contain: kill the child process tree, stop the affected PHP-FPM pool / w3wp app pool, isolate the host from the network, and block the source IP at the WAF. Patch CodeIgniter4 to >=4.7.3. 3) Hunt: enumerate every .php/.phar written by the webserver UID in the last 30d under docroot. Search outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the host for C2 candidates in the same time window. Audit the application's upload controllers for `$file->move($path)` calls that omit `getRandomName()`.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe","php-fpm","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","php.exe","php","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","caddy.exe","caddy")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","whoami.exe","whoami","id","uname","hostname.exe","hostname","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","ifconfig","ip","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","ps","wmic.exe","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","nc","ncat.exe","ncat","python.exe","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd","nginx","apache2","caddy")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","whoami","/id","uname","hostname","net.exe","ipconfig","ifconfig","systeminfo","tasklist","wmic","curl","wget","ncat","python","perl","ruby")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HTTP request to .php file under upload-style directory (webshell access pattern) AIExploitation Medium
Detects inbound HTTP requests targeting .php/.phtml/.phar files inside upload-style directories (uploads/, public/uploads/, writable/uploads/, files/). This is the call-the-shell step after CVE-2026-48062 exploitation places the polyglot file at a predictable URL. Rationale: Article-specific because CodeIgniter4 saves uploaded files via `$file->move($path)` using the original client filename - so the planted webshell sits at a URL the attacker chose and will fetch. Filtering for /uploads/, /public/uploads/, /writable/uploads/ (the exact path the advisory's workaround section recommends moving uploads OUT of) hits this exact failure mode. Defender Advanced Hunting has no inbound HTTP table so defender_kql is empty; Falcon FDR does not ship web access logs so falcon_logscale_query is empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised vulnerability scans (Nessus / Acunetix / Burp / OWASP ZAP) probing for arbitrary .php files in upload directories
  • Legitimate web file-manager applications (e.g. elFinder, KCFinder) that intentionally serve PHP from upload dirs
  • Static-asset CMSes that name images with .php in the path due to mod_rewrite oddities
  • Search-engine crawlers that have indexed exposed php files from prior misconfiguration
  • Internal red-team / pen-test traffic from known testing source IPs
Suppression filter
// Sentinel refinement - drop known scanner UAs and authorised pentest IPs
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","acunetix","Nuclei","Burp","OWASP ZAP","Qualys")
| where SrcIpAddr !in (dynamic(["<authorised-pentest-cidr>"]))
| where Url !contains "elfinder" and Url !contains "kcfinder"
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full request (URL, source IP, user agent, referer), verify the requested file exists on disk and inspect its contents - PHP code with image magic bytes confirms CVE-2026-48062 exploitation. Check the file's mtime against recent upload requests in the same log to identify the original POST that planted it. 2) Contain: delete the file from disk after preserving a forensic copy, block the source IP at the WAF/edge, and disable PHP execution in the upload directory via web-server config (the advisory's first workaround). Patch CodeIgniter4 to >=4.7.3. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP across all web logs for other probes / accesses. Sweep the entire web fleet for .php/.phar files under upload-style paths. Inspect application code for `$file->move(` without `getRandomName()` and for `ext_in[]` validation rules.
// Primary - ASIM web session table
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/(uploads?|public/uploads?|writable/uploads?|files|media)/[^/?#]+\.(php|phtml|phar|phps|pht)(\?|#|$)"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299) or HttpStatusCode between (300 .. 399)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode,
          HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpHostName, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
// Fallback - native IIS logs
// W3CIISLog

title: HTTP request to PHP file under upload directory (webshell access)
id: f4a2e1c8-7b3d-4f9e-a1c2-5d8e4b3a9f12
description: Detects inbound HTTP requests that fetch a .php/.phtml/.phar file from an upload-style directory (uploads/, public/uploads/, writable/uploads/, files/, media/). This is the call-the-shell step that follows a successful CVE-2026-48062 polyglot drop in CodeIgniter4 - the framework saves the upload under its client-supplied name into a web-accessible directory, leaving the webshell at a predictable URL.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
author: TI Pipeline
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|re: '(?i)/(uploads?|public/uploads?|writable/uploads?|files|media)/[^/]+\.(php|phtml|phar|phps|pht)$'
  filter_status:
    sc-status:
      - 404
      - 403
      - 401
  condition: selection and not filter_status
falsepositives:
  - Vulnerability scanners (Acunetix, Nessus, Burp Suite) probing during authorised tests
  - Legitimate file-manager apps that serve PHP from /uploads/

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GoFlateLoader Uses Massive PE Overlay to Deliver Lumma, Vidar, and StealC Infostealers

Cyber Security News
2026-06-11 2 use cases 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

A new malware loader called GoFlateLoader has been quietly spreading across the internet, and what makes it stand out is not how complex it is but how effective a simple trick has made it. Written in the Go programming language, this loader has one job: to decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs onto a victim&#8217;s [&#8230;] The post GoFlateLoader Uses Massive PE Overlay to Deliver Lumma, Vidar, and StealC Infostealers appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

"841c9297cb8a2e0ff89433d13c05bfc760eb2e98e251cb8fa785d2ad7cbac05f", "ece7c48eb411b24f26762ede83badb4a644c41d5777129381ac2541804d64fc2", "2415db5081cec9bfd14ad6da1a66169fd96f13a49010c319a73d1ed6fafd4efa", "d9917ade3b4c125a95b5d3e6343cde26145dfbf569bd7e2a843fd0c6fc8ddc28", "90ce4ff9da23ac150da0a8e17930cab1e369aa349fdc1b65691b70369145664a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b88c5744975d2abb447aecc6c090fee9f8580413f4612eecdc6ed1973e8a1739", "ed5ae7f36453c5a23e9868a5729d67e0549a11f6dea54f5f52d654a8f51d4902", "841c9297cb8a2e0ff89433d13c05bfc760eb2e98e251cb8fa785d2ad7cbac05f", "ece7c48eb411b24f26762ede83badb4a644c41d5777129381ac2541804d64fc2", "421ce2d2f49c23bbe9f60ef3b9cd38d7eb912ce02e56a61837656210069bd9e2", "121c2dc793b3873f75a29ec02241f94136de19c049382a50a50d0d5b99507073", "2415db5081cec9bfd14ad6da1a66169fd96f13a49010c319a73d1ed6fafd4efa", "d9917ade3b4c125a95b5d3e6343cde26145dfbf569bd7e2a843fd0c6fc8ddc28", "4cf6893756f441522b94b36f10e5de0e47aeed4743f95c51650746d1ecf97e3d", "8b89d6c9152d3aab97aadd515ecb69ca72654db2f25425759ba4b646853d737d", "90ce4ff9da23ac150da0a8e17930cab1e369aa349fdc1b65691b70369145664a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

AuditLogs

| where Result =~ "success"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Miasma/Hades dev-tool config dropped by non-IDE process (.claude/.cursor/.vscode/.gemini/.github) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the seven specific persistence files the StepSecurity write-up names (.claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, .vscode/tasks.json, .vscode/setup.mjs, .github/setup.js) being written by npm/node/python/pip/bun/git/PowerShell rather than by the editor itself. Legitimate developers create these via the IDE UI; worm propagation writes them via package install, git clone, or a downloader script. Rationale: Lifted the exact seven (file, tool, trigger) tuples from the article's Table 1 and combined with the observation that legitimate developers create these via the IDE GUI - never via npm/pip/git/cmd. StepSecurity, Snyk and Semgrep all corroborate the .vscode/.claude/.cursor file vector. The InitiatingProcess allowlist is the high-fidelity discriminator. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/ • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-miasma-and-hades-worms-target-bioinformatics-and-mcp-developers-via-malicious • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hades-pypi-attack-19-packages-poisoned.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Yeoman/create-react-app/cookiecutter scaffolding writing .vscode/settings.json into a freshly-generated project
  • git.exe writing .vscode/tasks.json or .github/setup.js while cloning a legitimate repo that ships those files (still worth a hunt - the repo may be the infection vector)
  • Internal devbox/devcontainer bootstrappers run via python.exe or PowerShell that hydrate IDE config from a central repo
  • Poetry/uv/pipx writing .vscode/settings.json on env init
  • Vendor-supplied repo templates legitimately containing .github/setup.js for workflow setup
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "git.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("clone","checkout")) // keep clone hits in a separate lower-severity stream
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","devcontainer.exe")) // IDE-launched scaffolding
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the FolderPath - is it inside a node_modules/site-packages dir, or at the repo root of a project the developer just cloned/opened? Check the file contents against the StepSecurity IOC bundle and the article's SHA256s. 2) Contain: isolate the host in Defender/Falcon, revoke any npm tokens (npm token list), PyPI tokens (~/.pypirc), GitHub PATs, and cloud creds reachable from that user via npm/pip/git - the worm reads these from process memory so consider them burned. 3) Hunt: across the fleet for the same FileName+SHA256, then DeviceProcessEvents for python.exe/node.exe spawning bun.exe, and AuditLogs for npm publish or git push bursts from the affected identity in the last 72h (self-propagation window).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" and FileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
   or  (FolderPath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and FileName =~ "setup.mdc")
   or  (FolderPath has @"\.gemini\" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or  (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
   or  (FolderPath has @"\.github\" and FileName =~ "setup.js")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.cmd","python.exe","python3.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","bun.exe","git.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\" and TargetFileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
   or  (TargetFilePath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.mdc")
   or  (TargetFilePath has @"\.gemini\" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json")
   or  (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\" and TargetFileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
   or  (TargetFilePath has @"\.github\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.js")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","python.exe","pip.exe","bun.exe","git.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phantom Gyp - tiny binding.gyp dropped into node_modules during npm install AIInstallation High
Hunts the 157-byte binding.gyp file Miasma v2 uses to trigger arbitrary code execution via node-gyp's native-build path, bypassing preinstall/postinstall lifecycle-script scanners. Detection is constrained to binding.gyp files in package-install locations with a file size band around the article's reported size and an npm/node-context writer. Rationale: Article names the exact technique 'Phantom Gyp' and pins the payload at 157 bytes - the size band 100-400 keeps the signal sharp while tolerating minor variants Semgrep observed across the 286 malicious versions. node_modules path scope keeps legit hand-authored binding.gyp at source-tree roots out of scope. Snyk and Chainguard both name binding.gyp + node-gyp invocation as the unique IOC. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/ • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://www.chainguard.dev/unchained/chainguard-artifacts-safe-from-miasma-phantom-gyp-npm-attack • https://socprime.com/active-threats/miasma-supply-chain-attack-spreads-through-the-phantom-gyp-worm/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native modules with very small binding.gyp stubs (rare but exist - flag and confirm manually)
  • npm cache restore replaying a binding.gyp from a tarball during CI provisioning
  • Yeoman generator scaffolding a new native node addon
  • Internal monorepo bootstrap regenerating package binding.gyp from template
  • Developer manually editing a tiny experimental binding.gyp at the root of a sandbox project (not under node_modules - already excluded by path filter)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure") and FolderPath has @"\node_modules\\.cache\\") // legitimate node-gyp cache rebuilds
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the binding.gyp contents - benign ones contain `targets` JSON with sources/include_dirs. Malicious Miasma payload embeds shell-out via gyp action/rules referencing node -e or curl. SHA256 against StepSecurity advisory and the article's IOC bundle (dc48b0..., e1342a..., etc.). 2) Contain: kill node-gyp processes on the host, isolate device, rotate npm/GitHub/cloud tokens for that user identity - assume they were read from process memory. Pull the package.json from the parent dir to identify the compromised package + version and pin the npm registry block. 3) Hunt: pivot on the parent package name across the org via DeviceFileEvents for the same node_modules path; check `npm publish` events from the affected user in the last 72h to scope self-propagation.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where FileSize between (100 .. 400)   // article: 157-byte payload
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\", @"\AppData\Roaming\npm\", @"\.npm\")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm.cmd","node.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where TargetFileSize between (100 .. 400)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\node_modules\", @"\AppData\Roaming\npm\", @"\.npm\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades on-import: python.exe spawns bun.exe / downloads Bun runtime from oven-sh AIInstallation High
Targets the Hades execution chain where an obfuscated one-liner in __init__.py downloads a standalone Bun runtime (bun.sh / github.com/oven-sh/bun) and runs a JS payload to read credentials from process memory. Detection joins a Bun-infrastructure network connection initiated by python/pip with a subsequent bun.exe child process within 5 minutes on the same host. Rationale: Article + Endor Labs + TheHackerNews confirm Hades downloads a standalone Bun runtime (avoiding any Node.js install requirement) and executes a JS payload triggered from __init__.py. The python-parent + bun-child pairing is essentially unheard-of in legitimate workflows; combining it with a temporally-near download from bun.sh / oven-sh/bun infra makes this a high-fidelity alert. SHA256 of bun.exe will not match the article IOCs because Bun itself is a legit signed binary - the malice is in the JS argv. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hades-pypi-attack-19-packages-poisoned.html • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/shai-hulud-hades-wave-hits-six-pypi-bioinformatics-packages • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-miasma-and-hades-worms-target-bioinformatics-and-mcp-developers-via-malicious • https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/hades-campaign-pypi-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007 T1195.002 T1552
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer evaluating Bun and bootstrapping it from a Python helper script
  • CI/CD pipeline that uses a Python orchestrator to fetch Bun for a cross-runtime build step (more common on build agents than dev hosts)
  • Internal devops tooling that wraps `bun install` inside a Python CLI
  • pip-installed package that genuinely depends on Bun (e.g. a JS-Python interop shim) - rare but possible
  • Developer running pip from within a Bun-managed shell where pwsh is the parent chain
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun create","bun install","bun upgrade") and BunPath has @"\AppData\Local\Programs\")  // user-managed bun install
| where not (Parent =~ "node.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe"))  // bun spawned via legitimate IDE task
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the bun.exe ProcessCommandLine - the argv exposes the JS payload URL or eval string Hades uses. Pull the originating __init__.py from the python.exe FolderPath / ProcessCommandLine and SHA256 it. Cross-check the PyPI package name against the article's list (ensmallen, embiggen, pyphetools, gpsea, phenopacket-store-toolkit, ppkt2synergy) and Endor Labs' wider IOC list. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill bun.exe and the parent python.exe, revoke npm/PyPI publish tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS/GCP/Azure CLI sessions, kubeconfigs, and HashiCorp Vault tokens reachable by that user - Hades reads them from process memory. Block bun.sh + registry.bun.sh egress on the corporate proxy as an interim control. 3) Hunt: across the fleet for any bun.exe spawned by python.exe in the last 14 days; pivot to UC5 to look for token-burst republish activity from the same identity.
let BunDownloads = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh","github.com/oven-sh/bun","registry.bun.sh","bun-windows-x64","bun-linux-x64","bun-darwin-x64")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python3.11.exe","python3.12.exe","python3.13.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget.exe")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, NetProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, NetCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let BunSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "bun.exe" or FolderPath endswith @"\bun.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python3.11.exe","python3.12.exe","python3.13.exe","pip.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
    | project ProcTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, BunPath = FolderPath, BunCmd = ProcessCommandLine, Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, AccountName;
BunDownloads
| join kind=inner BunSpawn on DeviceName
| where ProcTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + 5m)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project NetTime, ProcTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, NetTime), DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteUrl, NetProc, NetCmd, BunPath, BunCmd, Parent, ParentCmd, SHA256
| order by ProcTime desc
let BunDownloads = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any ("bun.sh","github.com/oven-sh/bun","registry.bun.sh","bun-windows-x64","bun-linux-x64","bun-darwin-x64")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Url, SrcUsername;
let BunSpawn = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "bun.exe" or TargetProcessName has "bun.exe"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","pip.exe")
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername;
BunDownloads
| join kind=inner BunSpawn on DvcHostname
| where ProcTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + 5m)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project NetTime, ProcTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ProcTime, NetTime), DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Url, BunCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, Parent = ParentProcessName
| order by ProcTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\PYTHON.EXE OR *\\pip.exe OR *\\PIP.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe) @Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\BUN.EXE OR *\\Bun.exe)

| ImageFileName=/\\bun\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(python3?(\.\d+)?|pip3?|node|powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i

IDE auto-load: VSCode/Cursor/Claude/Gemini spawns scripting host referencing Miasma persistence config AIExploitation Medium
Catches the on-open execution path: Code.exe/Cursor.exe/claude.exe/gemini.exe spawning node/powershell/cmd/bun/python where the command line or parent context contains one of the persistence file paths from the StepSecurity table (.vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen, .claude/setup.mjs SessionStart, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc on-load, etc.). This is the post-clone execution moment after UC1's file landed. Rationale: Each (IDE parent, scripting child, persistence-path cmdline marker) tuple is lifted directly from Table 1 of the article. The runOn:folderOpen / SessionStart triggers genuinely fire on project open in the legit case, so the cmdline path marker is what raises this above noise - without it the detection is unworkable, with it the detection only fires when the IDE is invoking one of the seven Miasma/Hades persistence files specifically. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-miasma-and-hades-worms-target-bioinformatics-and-mcp-developers-via-malicious • https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/hades-campaign-pypi-shai-hulud • https://www.scworld.com/news/mini-shai-hulud-hades-variant-affects-23-pypi-package-versions
ATT&CKT1546 T1059 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-authored .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen running legitimate lint/build steps
  • Devcontainer postCreateCommand spawning node setup scripts from .vscode/
  • Claude Code SessionStart hook installed by the developer themselves for legit local automation
  • Cursor rules pointing to a user-authored setup.mdc with project-bootstrap logic
  • Repo template that ships a benign .github/setup.js for org-mandated git hooks
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "devcontainer.exe")
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint","prettier","tsc --build","npm run lint","npm run format") and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","fetch(","eval(","atob(","base64")))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the child ProcessCommandLine and the referenced config file (`.vscode/tasks.json`, `.claude/setup.mjs`, etc.) on the host - benign ones are short and human-readable; Miasma/Hades versions contain heavily-obfuscated one-liners, fetch() to attacker infra, or eval of base64. SHA256 the config file against the StepSecurity advisory. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the child + IDE, snapshot the project directory for forensics, then rotate npm/PyPI/GitHub/cloud creds for the user. 3) Hunt: for every developer who opened the same repo (DeviceProcessEvents for `Code.exe` with the repo path in cmdline) in the last 14d - they're potentially infected even if they haven't run the tasks.json yet because folderOpen executes on first open.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode\\tasks.json",".vscode\\setup.mjs",".claude\\setup.mjs",".claude\\settings.json",".cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc",".gemini\\settings.json",".github\\setup.js")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)setup\.(mjs|mdc|js)"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode\\tasks.json",".vscode\\setup.mjs",".claude\\setup.mjs",".claude\\settings.json",".cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc",".gemini\\settings.json",".github\\setup.js")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)setup\.(mjs|mdc|js)"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(Code|Code - Insiders|Cursor|claude|claude-code|gemini)\.exe$/i
