Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

SecurityEvent

AI Broke Vulnerability Management. That's Why CISOs Are Moving Budget to BAS.

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 6 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

For thirty years, vulnerability management ran on a buffer: the months between when a vulnerability was found and when someone could figure out how to weaponize it. The solution was straightforward enough; triage by severity, schedule the fix, validate, and move on. The buffer was what made that work. Today, that buffer is gone. AI didn't make your team slower. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 15 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

Exploitation. Installation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe beaconing to SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callout (any process) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FireAnt Metakit supply-chain update: Metakit.exe spawns setup.exe (SPECTRALVIPER downloader) AIDelivery High
Hunts the first observable step of the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack: the legitimate Metakit.exe updater executing a tampered setup.exe pulled from metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml. Because Metakit.exe never validates the update binary's signature, an attacker-controlled setup.exe under this exact parent-child shape is the precise primitive ESET observed delivering SPECTRALVIPER. Rationale: Article names the EXACT legitimate binary (Metakit.exe), the EXACT malicious child filename (setup.exe), the update URL (metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml) lacking signature validation, and the post-execution HTTP POST to staging. Parent+child string pair is essentially unique to this campaign. Corroborated via ESET's welivesecurity report. Image #2 (figure of update flow) reinforced the chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine FireAnt Metakit updates after channel was cleaned (ESET reports no malicious updates since 2026-03-09 — anything from a confirmed-clean version is legitimate)
  • FireAnt internal QA test boxes that intentionally call the updater repeatedly
  • Symantec/Defender/AV scanning the dropped setup.exe (InitiatingProcessParentFileName chain would show explorer.exe → AV, not Metakit.exe → setup.exe)
  • An analyst sandbox detonating the IOC for triage
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","explorer.exe") and not (ProcessCommandLine has "/quiet" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\FireAnt\Sandbox\")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull SHA256 of the spawned setup.exe; compare against ESET's published IOC hashes. Pull the next 10 minutes of DeviceNetworkEvents for that host and look for HTTP POST to the C2 list. Confirm host runs a current Metakit version (compromise window: Oct 2025–Mar 2026). 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host via Defender Live Response. Quarantine setup.exe and any DtlCrashCatch.dll on disk. Block all six C2 domains and the eight IOC IPs at the proxy/firewall. Rotate any credentials cached on the host since Metakit.exe last ran. 3) HUNT: Pivot on FireAnt user population — every host in your estate running Metakit.exe is in scope. Search backwards 180 days for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe making outbound to any of the C2 domains (UC #3), and DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll across all hosts (UC #2).
let StagingDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let Drops = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA1, SHA256;
Drops
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "setup.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
    | where RemoteUrl has "metakit.fireant.vn" or RemoteUrl has_any (StagingDomains)
    | project DeviceId, NetTime = Timestamp, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
  ) on DeviceId
| where isnull(NetTime) or NetTime between (Timestamp - 10m .. Timestamp + 10m)
| order by Timestamp desc
let StagingDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Metakit.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\setup.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ProcessId
| join kind=leftouter (
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where Url has_any ("metakit.fireant.vn", StagingDomains)
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Url, DstIpAddr
  ) on Computer
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Updater Spawns setup.exe (SPECTRALVIPER Delivery)
id: 7c8f3a52-9b1d-4e7a-8c2f-1d6e4b3a8f59
status: experimental
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit legitimate updater (Metakit.exe) executing a child setup.exe — the exact parent-child shape used in the OceanLotus supply-chain compromise that delivered SPECTRALVIPER between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Metakit.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\setup.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate FireAnt Metakit updates after the channel was confirmed clean (post-2026-03-09)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\Metakit.exe OR *\METAKIT.EXE OR *\metakit.exe) @Image:(*\setup.exe OR *\SETUP.EXE OR *\Setup.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^Metakit\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" Processes.process_name="setup.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_path Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" Processes.process_name="setup.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_path Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load: DtlCrashCatch.dll image load or write AIInstallation High
Hunts the SPECTRALVIPER side-load primitive — image load or file write of the rogue DtlCrashCatch.dll. ESET names this exact DLL as the malicious side-loaded component dropped by the FireAnt downloader and as the entry point that injects SPECTRALVIPER into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. The string is unique enough to alert on a single hit. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is a campaign-unique string named explicitly in the ESET writeup. Searching DeviceImageLoadEvents and DeviceFileEvents for this filename surfaces both the side-load (load-time) and drop (write-time) primitives. No legitimate vendor product uses this filename — a single match is high-confidence. The article body explicitly identifies this DLL; ESET's welivesecurity page reinforces. ProcDump-style side-load mechanism was already established in Elastic's 2023 SPECTRALVIPER report. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1055.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • EDR/AV product scanning the DLL post-quarantine (LoadingProcess will be MsMpEng / SenseIR — excluded in the filter)
  • Threat-intel sandbox or malware analyst detonating an IOC sample on a research host
  • Backup software reading the file from disk (will appear as FileOpenInfo, not ImageLoad — different event class)
  • Defender Live Response operator pulling the artefact (InitiatingProcessFileName will be MsSense.exe)
Suppression filter
| where LoadingProcess !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe","WindowsDefender.exe","taskmgr.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Hash the on-disk DtlCrashCatch.dll, match against the 5 IOC SHA1s. Identify the LoadingProcess — ESET reports the legitimate signed binary varies, but the load almost always precedes OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe being injected, so check OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe outbound traffic within 5 minutes. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host. Quarantine the DLL and any sibling files in the same folder (the legitimate signed loader binary lives next to it). Kill OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe if it shows beaconing. 3) HUNT: Search Defender DeviceFileEvents for any file co-located with DtlCrashCatch.dll across the estate. Pivot on the LoadingProcess hash — the legitimate signed binary is being abused for side-load; finding other hosts running the same trio (signed binary + DtlCrashCatch.dll + injection target) identifies further victims.
union
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "ImageLoad", FilePath = FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,
              LoadingProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoadingProcessPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              LoadingProcessCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "FileWrite", FilePath = FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,
              LoadingProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoadingProcessPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              LoadingProcessCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| where LoadingProcessPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Windows Defender\"
     and LoadingProcessPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\"
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sysmon must be installed and forwarding (Image Load = EID 7, File Create = EID 11)
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
| where EventID in (7, 11)
| where EventData has "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| extend EvtType = case(EventID == 7, "ImageLoad", "FileCreate")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EvtType, EventID, EventData, ParameterXml
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SPECTRALVIPER Side-Loaded DtlCrashCatch.dll Image Load
id: 3d4a8b1f-2e6c-4a9d-b8e3-5f7c1a9b6d24
status: experimental
description: Detects image load of DtlCrashCatch.dll — the rogue DLL ESET observed side-loaded in OceanLotus campaigns to inject SPECTRALVIPER into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe.
references:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(7 OR 11) (@ImageLoaded:(*\DtlCrashCatch.dll OR *\dtlcrashcatch.dll OR *\DTLCRASHCATCH.DLL) OR @TargetFilename:(*\DtlCrashCatch.dll OR *\dtlcrashcatch.dll OR *\DTLCRASHCATCH.DLL))

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe beaconing to SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure AICommand & Control High
Hunts the post-injection behaviour ESET observed — SPECTRALVIPER running inside the injected OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process and contacting financemachinelearning[.]com or gatewayrvcenter[.]com for C2. OneDrive's legitimate sync service exclusively talks to Microsoft domains; an outbound connection to a non-Microsoft host (especially the ESET-named C2s) is a direct injection-and-beacon signal. Rationale: ESET names OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe as the specific injection target and financemachinelearning[.]com / gatewayrvcenter[.]com as the active C2s. The combination is high-fidelity: a Microsoft-signed process making outbound calls to non-Microsoft destinations is, by itself, anomalous; matching the named C2s is conclusive. IOC IPs/domains added from the pre-extracted list to cover additional infrastructure pivots ESET likely published. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1055
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe legitimately connecting only to *.microsoft.com / *.live.com / *.onedrive.com — these are NOT in the C2 list so the IOC-bound query excludes them by construction
  • Third-party security tool resolving the C2 domains under OneDrive's process context (extremely unusual — security tools run under their own service)
  • Analyst manually pinging the C2 from a hunting box for triage
  • Sinkholed IPs returning the IOC IPs from a takedown — distinguishable by passive DNS check
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the connecting process is genuinely OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (check SHA256 against Microsoft's signed hash). Pull the last 30 minutes of DeviceImageLoadEvents on the host for DtlCrashCatch.dll loads — that confirms the injection. Capture a memory snapshot of the OneDrive process before containment for malware analysis. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response. Block the matched C2 domain at the proxy. Kill the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process; legitimate sync will respawn from MsSense, the injected one will not. Force credential rotation for the logged-on user. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the resolved RemoteIP and search DeviceNetworkEvents across the estate for any process connecting to it (not just OneDrive). Look for the parent FireAnt Metakit setup.exe execution (UC #1) in the prior 30 days on this host. Sweep all hosts for DtlCrashCatch.dll (UC #2).
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains) or RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
     or (isempty(RemoteUrl) and not(RemoteUrl endswith ".live.com") and not(RemoteUrl endswith ".microsoft.com") and not(RemoteUrl endswith ".office.com") and not(RemoteUrl endswith ".sharepoint.com") and not(RemoteUrl endswith ".onedrive.com"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where SrcUsername has "OneDrive.Sync.Service" or Url has "OneDrive.Sync.Service"
| where DstHostname has_any (C2Domains) or DstIpAddr in (C2IPs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| union (
    Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
    | where EventData has "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
    | where EventData has_any (C2Domains) or EventData has_any (C2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, EventData
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe Beacons to SPECTRALVIPER C2
id: 9e1f5c83-4b2a-4d8c-a7f1-3e9b5d2c8f47
status: experimental
description: Detects OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe contacting one of the OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains. Legitimate OneDrive sync exclusively talks to Microsoft hosts; any of these destinations indicates the process has been injected with SPECTRALVIPER.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1055
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe'
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'financemachinelearning.com'
      - 'gatewayrvcenter.com'
      - 'coachcybersecurity.com'
      - 'mxprodesign.com'
      - 'power-sync-services.com'
      - 'leadingfilipinoteams.com'
  selection_ip:
    Image|endswith: '\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe'
    DestinationIp:
      - '38.60.245.37'
      - '139.99.33.239'
      - '139.162.11.152'
      - '139.180.128.42'
      - '142.91.98.77'
      - '166.88.77.186'
      - '194.68.26.241'
      - '103.119.47.104'
  condition: selection or selection_ip
falsepositives:
  - Vanishingly rare — OneDrive sync exclusively talks to Microsoft domains
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe OR *\onedrive.sync.service.exe OR *\ONEDRIVE.SYNC.SERVICE.EXE) (@DestinationHostname:(financemachinelearning.com OR gatewayrvcenter.com OR coachcybersecurity.com OR mxprodesign.com OR power-sync-services.com OR leadingfilipinoteams.com) OR @DestinationIp:(38.60.245.37 OR 139.99.33.239 OR 139.162.11.152 OR 139.180.128.42 OR 142.91.98.77 OR 166.88.77.186 OR 194.68.26.241 OR 103.119.47.104))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest) ContextImageFileName=/\\OneDrive\.Sync\.Service\.exe$/i
| (DomainName=/^(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i OR RemoteAddressIP4=/^(38\.60\.245\.37|139\.99\.33\.239|139\.162\.11\.152|139\.180\.128\.42|142\.91\.98\.77|166\.88\.77\.186|194\.68\.26\.241|103\.119\.47\.104)$/)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" AND (All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104") OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" AND (All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104") OR All_Traffic.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callout (any process) AICommand & Control High
Broad-spectrum hunt for any process on any host contacting the SPECTRALVIPER C2 domain or IP list named by ESET, including the second campaign's gatewayrvcenter[.]com (Vietnamese transport construction corp). Catches SPECTRALVIPER variants where the injection target differs from OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, and the loader stages that beacon before injection completes. Rationale: Six C2 domains and eight IPs explicitly tied to OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER infrastructure across both campaigns. financemachinelearning[.]com and gatewayrvcenter[.]com are named directly in the ESET article body; the remaining four domains and the IPs come from the pre-extracted IOC bundle and align with the broader campaign infrastructure. Two distinct kill-chain campaigns share this list, so any hit warrants alerting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VirusTotal / urlscan / Hybrid Analysis reputation lookups from analyst workstations (filter on SOC subnet)
  • Threat-intel feed processors hitting the domains to enrich indicators (filter on TIP service accounts)
  • Sandbox detonations in security research VMs
  • Sinkholed IPs after takedown returning legitimate-looking traffic for retrospective post-mortem
  • Vendor EDR threat-feed validation calls
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","vt-cli.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Determine if the connecting host runs FireAnt Metakit (FireAnt campaign scope) or has a public-facing MSSQL server (transport construction corp scope). Pull the InitiatingProcess and check whether it's OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (UC #3 territory), Metakit.exe / setup.exe (UC #1), or sqlservr.exe (initial-access pivot). 2) CONTAIN: Block all six domains and all eight IPs at the proxy/firewall immediately — they cover both campaigns. Isolate the host. Hash any binaries in InitiatingProcessFolderPath and compare against the UC #5 SHA1 list. 3) HUNT: Pivot from each matched IP using passive DNS — adversary may use additional FQDNs not in this list. Search the previous 180 days for the same RemoteIP across all hosts. Run UC #2 (DtlCrashCatch.dll) and UC #5 (SHA1 match) estate-wide.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains) or RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            HitCount = count(),
            Procs = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 32),
            Cmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 32),
            Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 16),
            Destinations = make_set(coalesce(RemoteUrl, tostring(RemoteIP)), 16)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen asc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains) or DestinationIP in (C2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where Name has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER / FireAnt downloader SHA1 IOC hash hunt AIInstallation Medium
Retroactive hunt for the five SHA1 hashes published with the OceanLotus FireAnt / transport construction campaigns. Covers execution, file write, and image load — catches the downloader, the side-loaded DLL, and the SPECTRALVIPER payload variants ESET captured during the 2024-2026 intrusions. Rationale: Five SHA1 hashes from the pre-extracted IOC bundle covering the OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER tooling. Targeting process create + file write + image load gives the widest possible retroactive coverage — catches the downloader (UC #1), the side-loaded DLL (UC #2), and the SPECTRALVIPER payload binaries. ESET's welivesecurity report is the authoritative source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1027 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike / VT scanning the IOC samples after analyst submission — InitiatingProcessFileName will be MsMpEng / SenseIR / etc.
  • Malware-analysis sandbox VMs detonating the samples (filter on the sandbox host subnet)
  • Threat-intel platform retroactively pulling samples from a malware feed
  • Endpoint full-disk hash inventory job hitting a quarantined sample
Suppression filter
| where ParentImage !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe","vt-cli.exe","7zG.exe","7z.exe") and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine\"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: For each hit, identify the file path and parent process. Pull EventClass: ProcessCreate hits are 'live execution' (highest severity); FileWrite is 'on disk' (still concerning if recent); ImageLoad means a process actively side-loaded the artefact. Check whether the host runs FireAnt Metakit or has public-facing MSSQL. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate every host with a match. Quarantine the file using Defender Live Response. Add the SHA1s to your tenant indicator block-list to prevent re-execution. Capture memory of any process whose image was the matched hash. 3) HUNT: For each hit, pivot on the surrounding 1-hour window — pull DeviceNetworkEvents (UC #4 C2 list), DeviceProcessEvents for child processes spawned by the matched binary, and DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll. Sweep the estate for the same file name and same parent process chain on other hosts.
let KnownSha1 = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"
]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "ProcessCreate", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let KnownSha1 = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1) or Hash in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EvtType = "ProcessCreate", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA1),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in (KnownSha1) or Hash in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EvtType = "FileWrite", TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName),
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where FileHash has_any (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, EvtType = "4688", NewProcessName, CommandLine, FileHash),
  (ThreatIntelligenceIndicator
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where FileHashValue in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = "(TI match)", EvtType = "ThreatIntel", IndicatorId, FileHashValue, ThreatType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

            - 'wget '

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 6 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
